a.summary: MAIN FIX LOST. Commit 7377486 added the `serializedSignatureCount` record component so `requireSignableSignatureLayout()` can reject parsed messages whose serialized signature vector disagrees with the header. v1_tx wrote its constructor against the merge-base component list, and because main only touched the record header (hunk 1) while v1_tx replaced the whole declaration, git dropped the component with no conflict. Without it the guard restored in hunk 6 does not compile, and the signing-boundary hardening is silently reverted.

b.summary: MAIN FIX LOST. Commit 7377486 added the `serializedSignatureCount` record component so `requireSignableSignatureLayout()` can reject parsed messages whose serialized signature vector disagrees with the header. v1_tx wrote its constructor against the merge-base component list, and because main only touched the record header (hunk 1) while v1_tx replaced the whole declaration, git dropped the component with no conflict. Without it the guard restored in hunk 6 does not compile, and the signing-boundary hardening is silently reverted. Verified safe: the `TransactionSkeleton` interface declares no `serializedSignatureCount()` or `messageOffset()` accessor, and no test calls either on a skeleton, so a private field is a complete replacement for the record component.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
